key: What time hath past since they were first set flowing?
s: Opening a hymn chiefly to Indra, the verse tells of waters that never rest from flowing; Sāyaṇa, on 2.30.1, takes the question as a dismissal, since the waters are eternal and there was no first time to measure.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa, on Rig Veda 2.30.1, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 213335 (2019)

opened.locator: 2.30.1 and its note on the drift of the question

evidence.words: आसां प्रथमः सर्गः प्राथमिकं जन्म कियात्या । कियति काले निष्पन्नं । आकारः प्रश्ने । किंशब्द आक्षेपे । यावति काले ता अजायंत स कालः कियान् । किं परिमाणं तस्य कालस्य । न किमपि । नित्या एव हि ता इत्यर्थः ।
evidence.gloss: Their first creation (sargaḥ), their first birth: in how long a time (kiyātyā) was it brought about? The ā marks a question; the word kim is used in dismissal. The time in which they were born, how long is it? What is the measure of that time? None at all. For they are eternal: that is the meaning.
